heading: The `for call` stub
text:
### The `for call` stub [LTSL.7.2]

A stub is:

```
for call <service>[.<method>] [slot: val …] [as "<corr>"] [after <dur>]:
    <reply fact>          # one or more constructed facts, or
    no response
```

The stub keys on the outbound call — by its correlation (`as "<corr>"`) or by
argument equality (`slot: val`, [LTSL.4.3]). A stub **must** identify the call by correlation or
arguments (`DS_VALIDATE_TEST_STUB_UNKEYED`), because its reply must carry the matching `corr`; a bare service match is
reserved for the `called` assertion ([LTSL.8]), which has no reply to mis-key.

**A reply may omit `corr`, and the test runner supplies it.** When a reply fact
writes no `corr`, the test runner **must** give it the correlation of the call the
stub matched: the call's `as` value, or the value generated for it
([LCCO.3.4]), which a test cannot know when it is written. A `corr` the reply
writes is kept as written, so a test can answer under another correlation on
purpose. `corr` is the one slot a constructed fact may leave out ([LTSL.4.1]).
